title: Fylgja API, version 1
description: M13: what crosses the API beside the documents Fylgja already versions. A request is $defs/request with the args of its operation ($defs/args). An answer is application/x-ndjson, each line one $defs/frame, the last a document frame whose document is findings.schema.json's, unchanged at findings_version 1. A transport fault's body is $defs/problem. The snapshot (the CTM before 018), the bundle and a support package cross inside $defs/file, as bytes, and are validated by their own schemas (snapshot.schema.json, manifest.schema.json, psp.schema.json), never here. No token, login, configuration line or device diff appears in any of these. 014: the operations stage.list and stage.plan replace waypoint.list and waypoint.plan, and twin.create, twin.step and intent.read take stage where they took waypoint; the version stays 1, since the API is pre-1.0 and every other operation is unchanged. 015: the operation twin.rehearse (its args the branch; an interrupt from its start, whose workflow is fylgja-rehearse), and the rendering markdown, whose document frame carries the report as markdown beside its text on twin.rehearse alone; the version stays 1, since a client of M13 ignores a new operation, a render value it does not send and a frame field it does not know. 017: twin.create, twin.rehearse, intent.read, stage.plan and stage.list take scope, tag:<name>, the devices every read of the request selects; the version stays 1, since a client that never sends it is served under the server's default scope. twin.step takes none: it reads under the scope its twin's record carries. 018: the snapshot crosses where the CTM did, in twin.compile's request, as twin.create's one file beside a snapshot that is a path, and in intent.read's files frame (snapshot.json), each validated by snapshot.schema.json; twin.create and twin.compile take snapshot, and twin.compile no longer takes ctm; the version stays 1, since a client that never sends snapshot is served as before, and the API is pre-1.0, as 014 renamed series to stage. 019: twin.create takes neither interval nor no_follow, since a twin follows nothing (D-062), and a request carrying either is refused as any argument not taken; the version stays 1, pre-1.0, as 018 removed twin.compile's ctm. twin.step takes snapshot, its target, a snapshot id or the path of the file the request carries, as twin.create's; the version stays 1, since a client that never sends it is served as before. 016: intent.read, twin.create, twin.step, stage.plan and twin.rehearse take probes, the path of a probe declaration (probes.schema.json) the request carries as its one file under that path, as twin.create's snapshot file crosses; the server reads it once at the request's start, in place of the probes declared in FylgjaProbe on the default branch, and every snapshot the request takes carries that one list; a request naming probes with no file, or a file under another path, is 400, the request is not one; beside snapshot on twin.create and twin.step it is snapshot.flags.conflict at --probes, since a snapshot carries its own list; the version stays 1, since a client that never sends it is served with the kind's probes, or none. 020: twin.create, twin.provision, twin.step and twin.destroy take detach, under which the answer ends at the run's identity, its start, its run and a document naming run.detached, and the run goes on; the operations run.read and run.interrupt (their args workflow_id and run_id) reach a run of fylgja-provision, fylgja-step or fylgja-destroy by its identity, and the run frame gains state, on run.read alone; a run.read of a run still running ends by EOF after its run and events, the one answer whose last line is not a document frame; the operation twin.diff (its args from and to, each a snapshot id or the path of a snapshot file the request carries) answers the step between two snapshots and starts nothing; the version stays 1, since a client that never sends detach is answered as before and a client ignores a field and an operation it does not know. 020 also removes what read Infrahub, which the orchestrator's adapter reads (D-065): the operations twin.rehearse, stage.list, stage.plan, intent.read and schema.check, each path answering 404 as one the version has no operation at, without Fylgja-Api-Versions; the arguments branch, at, stage, scope and probes of twin.create and twin.step, each refused as any argument not taken, so both take snapshot alone of what names their intent; the start frame's fylgja-rehearse, the probe file and intent.read's files frame; the version stays 1, pre-1.0, as 019 removed interval and no_follow.

render.description: The rendering the client asks for beside the document: text is what the command printed without --json at M12; json is what it wrote to stderr under --json; markdown (015) is text's frames, every operation answering it as it answers text (twin.rehearse's document frame carried its markdown beside its text until 020 removed the operation). Absent: no out or err frame and no document text.

args.description: The command's arguments as given, one of $defs/args by the operation the path names. An absent key is a flag that was not given.

files.description: twin.create: the snapshot, under the path snapshot gives, when snapshot is a path (018). twin.step: the same, the target's snapshot (019). twin.compile: the snapshot, under the path given (018; the CTM before it). twin.provision: every regular file of the bundle directory, each under its slash-separated path inside it. psp.validate: each package, under the path given, in order. twin.diff (020): the snapshot file of each of from and to that is not a snapshot id, under that path, a path both name carried once.

args.description: The arguments of each operation. Every key is optional on the wire but three: a required flag that is missing is refused by the server under M12's identifier and wording. twin.provision's bundle, which M12's command took as its one argument, is required, twin.verify's args are given only beside wait, and run.read's and run.interrupt's workflow_id (020), which their commands always send, is required; the server refuses a request without any of them as 400, the request is not one.

snapshot.description: --snapshot as given: a snapshot id (64 lowercase hex characters) the store holds, or the path of the file the request carries; absent, refused --snapshot is required (020)

detach.description: --detach (020): the answer ends at the run's start, its run and a document naming run.detached, and the run goes on, read by run.read and interrupted by run.interrupt; beside dry_run, refused run.flags.conflict

bundle.description: The bundle directory as the operator gave it, for the subject and every sentence that names it. The server opens no path a client names.

detach.description: --detach (020): the answer ends at the run's start, its run and a document naming run.detached, and the run goes on, read by run.read and interrupted by run.interrupt; beside dry_run, refused run.flags.conflict

snapshot.description: --snapshot as given (019): the target, a snapshot id (64 lowercase hex characters) the store holds, or the path of the file the request carries; absent, refused step.target.unknown (020)

wait.description: --wait as given; present and empty is --wait=

detach.description: --detach (020): the answer ends at the run's start, its run and a document naming run.detached, and the run goes on, read by run.read and interrupted by run.interrupt; beside dry_run, refused run.flags.conflict

--detach (020): the answer ends at the destroy run's start, its run, which a followed destroy's answer never carries, and a document naming run.detached, and the run goes on; what the destroy cancels first is still waited for

wait.description: --wait's value: the default budget when the flag was given bare

args.description: The words a bare --wait leaves as arguments, which the server refuses as verify.wait.invalid

snapshot.description: --snapshot as given: the path of the snapshot file the request carries, under that path (018; ctm before it, which is no argument of this operation)

workflow_id.description: --workflow as given (020): fylgja-provision, fylgja-step or fylgja-destroy; any other, the empty string included, is refused run.unknown before anything is dialled

run_id.description: --run as given (020): the run's id; absent is the workflow's latest run

workflow_id.description: --workflow as given (020): fylgja-provision, fylgja-step or fylgja-destroy; any other, the empty string included, is refused run.unknown before anything is dialled

run_id.description: --run as given (020): the run's id; absent is the workflow's latest run

from.description: --from as given (020): the snapshot the step goes from, a snapshot id (64 lowercase hex characters) the store holds, or the path of the file the request carries; absent, refused --from is required

to.description: --to as given (020): the snapshot the step goes to, as from; absent, refused --to is required

frame.description: One line of an answer. A frame's kind is its key. A client ignores a kind it does not know. The last line is a document frame, but on a run.read of a run still running (020), which ends after its run and events.

out.description: Text for stdout, whole lines, as M12 printed them. Under render text, and under render markdown (015), which prints the same lines.

err.description: Text for stderr, whole lines. Under every rendering.

start.description: The server begins to start this run. From here an interrupt call reaches it, on an operation that takes one: twin.destroy's start opens no stream, and its followed answer has no run frame; under detach (020) it has one, after the start. fylgja-rehearse, twin.rehearse's, left with the operation (020).

files.description: twin.compile: every file of the bundle, each under its path inside it. (intent.read's one file, snapshot.json, left with the operation, 020.)

text.description: Under render text or markdown, when the document has findings: they as text, for stderr, as M12's report printed them.

markdown.description: 015: under render markdown, on twin.rehearse alone, the report as GitHub-flavoured markdown, rendered from the document and the plan's steps; a rendering, never part of the document. From 020, which removed twin.rehearse, absent on every operation and rendering; the orchestrator's rehearse flow renders the report.

state.description: 020: on run.read alone, the run's state as the workflow service describes it. running: the answer ends after the run's events so far, by EOF, with no document; any other: the run has closed, and the answer ends with the document its result makes, or the operation failing at the step its history reached when it closed without one. Absent on every other operation's run frame.

event.description: One step boundary of a run, or one notice about a run, read from the run's history (M2's progress event).

step.description: As the progress line names it: read, readiness n1, cleanup teardown

finding_step.description: The step as findings name it, when it has one

problem.description: The body of a transport fault: 401, 404, 413, 400, 409. The status says which.
